title: A Demonstration of Correaltion Analysis in Python & Quarto
text:
Introduction

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

sns.set_context('talk')

df = sns.load_dataset('iris')

For at least five minutes researchers at UW-Madison’s DSHB program have had an interest in learning more about correlations in the iris data from Seaborn. Our program will use this topic as a demonstration of working with correlation analysis in Python and Quarto; we have data from 150 flowers and our research question is to study whether the petal width correlates with petal length.


Literature Review
The data for our analysis was originally published by Unwin and Kleinman (2021). While typically these data are often used to demonstrate classification methods we use it to demonstrate correaltion analysis.


Method
Given that we have two columns of continuous data (length of petal and width of petal measured in millimeters) we will evaluate this relationship using simple correalation analysis and also a scatterplot. These two methods are classic and traditional starting points when evaluating data like these.


Results

corr_val = np.array(df[['petal_length', 'petal_width']].corr())[0][1]

narrative = "a very strong negative correlation"

if corr_val > .8:
    narrative = "a very strong positive correlation"
elif corr_val > .4:
    narrative = "a moderate positive correlation"
elif corr_val > 0:
    narrative = "a positive but weak correlation"
elif corr_val > -.4:
    narrative = "a moderate negative correlation"

Using the classic simple Pearson correaltion approach these data produce a correlation coefficient of 0.96287, as such, given this result we conclude that the relationship is a very strong positive correlation.

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5))

sns.scatterplot(data=df, y='petal_length', x='petal_width')

plt.ylabel('Petal Width (mm)')
plt.xlabel('Petal Length (mm)')







Figure 1: A scatterplot of petal length and width





As shown in Figure 1 we see additional evidence of a strong positive correlation between an iris flower petal length and petal width.


Discussion
Now that this long-standing problem (of over 10 minutes) is resolved (thanks to the diligent efforts of UW-Madison’s DSHB program) science has once again triumphed in establishing that there is a positive correlative relationship between iris petal width and iris petal length as a matter of empircally certain ground truth. The end (because we needed a second sentence).
